summary:
MODIS–VIIRS Fire Watch is an end-to-end wildfire monitoring, forecasting, and early-warning system centered on four integrated components: 

(1) a formal harmonization paper and specification (harmonization.md) detailing the Single Source of Truth (SSOT) physics and statistical logic that reconciles NASA FIRMS 1 km MODIS and 375 m VIIRS detections across sensor lifecycle asymmetry, elliptical GIFOV (scan x track) geometry, bow-tie distortion, non-additive FRP ratios, and orbital time delays

(2) a web-based 3D Next.js + Mapbox GL dashboard applying the harmonized SSOT stream alongside an interactive 14D DAILY SSOT and 2001–2026 MONTHxYEAR Fire Activity Calendar, t0 hindcast validation, and provenance-stamped CSV exports

(3) scikit-learn ML models connected directly to the dashboard and harmonized fire tracks to predict 0–100 hazard ratings, 12–24 hour persistence, and spread/expansion envelopes

(4) a low-cost hardware alerting solution that interfaces directly with the platform's APIs and predictive models to dispatch immediate warnings to nearby authorities and first responders whenever hazardous or rapidly expanding fires are predicted.

PROJECT OVERVIEW

An end-to-end wildfire harmonization, forecasting, and early-warning system comprising four core components:

1. Harmonization Paper & Methodology: Formalizes the physics- and statistics-driven Single Source of Truth (SSOT) logic reconciling NASA FIRMS MODIS (~1 km, 2000–present) and VIIRS (~375 m, 2012–present) detections across operational lifecycle asymmetry, elliptical GIFOV (scan x track) geometry, bow-tie distortion, non-additive FRP ratios, and orbital time delays (Δt).

2. Web-Based 3D Geospatial Dashboard: A Next.js and Mapbox GL platform applying the harmonized SSOT dataset (SSOT · HARMONIZED), real-time active/past fire inspection, 14D DAILY SSOT + 2001–2026 MONTHxYEAR Fire Activity Calendars, on-map t0 hindcasts, and provenance-stamped CSV exports.

Web Dashboard:

3. Scikit-Learn ML Forecasting Pipeline: Connected to our dashboard and harmonized detection streams to compute composite 0–100 Hazard Ratings alongside calibrated 12–24 hour Persistence, Spread/Expansion Probability, and Additional Area Envelope forecasts.

4. Low-Cost Hardware Alerting Solution: A cost-effective physical edge/field alerting unit that interfaces directly with our platform APIs and ML hazard/spread models to warn nearby authorities and first responders immediately when high-risk or expanding hazardous fires are predicted.

Its software pipeline operates through a Two-Pipe Architecture:

- Pipe A : 3-Pillar Single Source of Truth (SSOT) Harmonization (SSOT · HARMONIZED): Reconciles operational lifecycle asymmetry (2000–2026), optical lens & elliptical GIFOV geometry (scan x track, 375 m vs. 1 km, MODIS bow-tie distortion), non-additive FRP reconciliation, 3-regime temporal (Δt) deduplication, overpass-aware MODIS false-alarm gating, LOO-CV statistical calibration, and an interactive 14D DAILY SSOT + 2001–2026 MONTHxYEAR Fire Activity Calendar with CSV exports.

- Pipe B : Isolated 14-Day Fire Tracking, VIIRS ML Prediction & t0 Hindcasts: Preserves three independent 14-day tracker runs (SSOT · HARMONIZED, VIIRS · ML, MODIS), Pakistan-calibrated VIIRS Hazard (0–100) and scikit-learn spread models (Models 1–3), and on-map t0 Past-Fire Hindcast Validation (Initial Pass vs. Actual vs. Model Predicted Spread).

ARCHITECTURE & END-TO-END WORKFLOW

1. FIRMS Ingestion & Dataset Reference Anchor:

Retrieves 14-day MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) NRT and archive detections inside country boundaries, normalizes UTC acquisition timestamps, extracts scan x track footprint dimensions in kilometers, and anchors the reference window to the latest in-country detection timestamp (splitting active fires <=12h from past fires >12h).

2. Pipe B — Three Independent 14-Day Fire Tracker Runs:

Executes three isolated 14-day fire tracking passes:

- SSOT · HARMONIZED Tab: Tracks combined MODIS + VIIRS events, attaches VIIRS ML forecasts strictly to VIIRS-evidenced fires, and tags each event with its SSOT reconciliation provenance.

- VIIRS · ML Tab: Tracks pure VIIRS detections to power the 0–100 Hazard Rating, 12–24 hour persistence/spread models, and initial-pass (t0) hindcasts.

- MODIS Tab: Tracks pure MODIS detections with VIIRS-trained ML disabled to prevent cross-sensor feature distortion.

3. Pipe A — Physical & Temporal SSOT Reconciliation:

Evaluates elliptical GIFOV (scan x track + 0.25 km geolocation uncertainty) containment, applies 3-regime temporal (Δt) gating (coincident dual confirmations, diurnal bridged passes, solo sub-resolution VIIRS, solo MODIS gap-fill, and overpass-aware MODIS false-alarm demotion), computes non-additive FRP diagnostics, suppresses redundant 1 km MODIS duplicate centroids, and links each canonical hotspot to its tracked fire event.

4. Pipe A — Statistical Calibration & 2001–2026 Climatology:

Applies cross-sensor confidence filtering (MODIS >= 30%, VIIRS nominal/high), flags local solar overpass families and late-afternoon orbital drift, aggregates detections into sensor-neutral 1 km (0.009°) and 0.25° hotspot-cell-day bins, fits a log-linear VIIRS-to-MODIS-equivalent transfer model with Leave-One-Day-Out Cross-Validation (LOO-CV) and 90% prediction intervals, and constructs a 2001–2026 Month x Year climatology series overlaying live FIRMS observations onto the historical seasonal baseline.

5. Synchronized 3D Globe, Sidebar HUD & Fire Activity Calendar:

Renders tier-aware Mapbox layers (including amber GIFOV halos for MODIS gap-fill footprints and dimmed opacity for demoted anomalies), synchronizes the 5-step Harmonization Filter, 24-hour orbital pass scrubber, and multi-day calendar range selections across the map and sidebar, and displays on-map Past Fire Hindcast rings comparing initial-pass (t0) footprints, observed actual spread, and model-predicted spread.

SIDEBAR:

PIPE A: 3-PILLAR SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (SSOT) HARMONIZATION STRATEGY

Why boolean splitting (VIIRS only, MODIS only, MODIS + VIIRS) and naive pixel subdivision fail:

1. A fire covering only a small fraction of a pixel can trigger a 1 km MODIS detection, so subdividing 1 km MODIS pixels into synthetic 375 m cells invents phantom fires and inflates burned area up to 900%.

2. Counting raw co-located MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) points or summing their FRP double-counts the exact same thermal anomaly.

3. Uncoordinated MODIS (~10:30 Terra & drifting ~13:30+ Aqua) vs. VIIRS (~13:30 S-NPP/N20/N21) overpasses turn real diurnal fire persistence (~3h apart) into apparent disagreement unless time delays are explicitly modeled.

Our Pipe A SSOT engine resolves all three physics asymmetries:

Pillar 1 — Operational Lifecycle Asymmetry (2000–2026 & Climatology)

- MODIS Terra: ~1 km nadir (~2 x 4.8 km edge), ~10:30 / 22:30 local solar overpass. Morning/night anchor since 2000; bridges morning starts before afternoon VIIRS passes.

- MODIS Aqua: ~1 km nadir (~2 x 4.8 km edge), ~13:30 / 01:30 local solar overpass (drifting). Afternoon archive continuity since 2002; orbital drift flagged automatically.

- VIIRS (S-NPP, N20, N21): ~375 m nadir (~0.75 x 0.75 km edge), ~13:30 / 01:30 local solar overpass. Sub-resolution sensitivity & onboard bow-tie deletion since 2012.

- Cross-Sensor Statistical Baseline: Filters to MODIS >= 30% confidence and VIIRS nominal/high (n/h), deduplicates into 0.009° (~1 km) and 0.25° hotspot-cell-day bins, records canonical ssotFrpSum (eliminating dual-sensor FRP double-counting), and tracks daily SSOT regime counts (coincident dual, diurnal bridged, sub-resolution VIIRS, MODIS gap-fill, demoted anomalies).

- Transfer Calibration & Validation: Calibrates VIIRS -> MODIS-equivalent cell-days via log-linear regression regularized toward the empirical 0.34 prior, reporting LOO-CV MAE, RMSE, bias, R², quality flags, and 90% prediction intervals.

- 2001–2026 Month x Year Climatology: Separates the MODIS era (2001–2011) and Overlap era (2012–2026), overlays live/queried FIRMS cells onto the regional historical curve, and computes out-of-sample monthly median, IQR, anomaly ratio, percentile, peak months, and peak years.

Pillar 2 — Optical Lens, Elliptical GIFOV Geometry & Bow-Tie Mitigation

1. Actual scan x track Elliptical Containment: Rather than a fixed 1.0 km circle, MODIS–VIIRS matching evaluates whether the 375 m VIIRS point lies inside the actual off-nadir MODIS elliptical Ground Instantaneous Field of View (semi-axis = 0.5 x scan/track + 0.25 km geolocation uncertainty), neutralizing MODIS swath-edge stretching (~4.8 km x 2.0 km, 50% consecutive scan overlap) and complementing VIIRS onboard bow-tie deletion (3x1 -> 2x1 -> 1x1).

2. Spatial Lock & MODIS Suppression: Any VIIRS pixels falling inside a corroborating MODIS GIFOV lock the SSOT spatial geometry to the sharper 375 m VIIRS coordinates (Tier 1) and suppress the redundant 1 km MODIS container centroid, storing corroborated MODIS metadata on the surviving detection.

3. Non-Additive FRP Reconciliation: Overlapping sensors measure radiative power across different background apertures; SSOT never adds co-located MODIS + VIIRS FRP together. It reports canonical FRP alongside the diagnostic ratio FRP_M / Σ FRP_V.

4. Footprint Halo Rendering: Tier 3 MODIS Gap-Fill nodes keep their true footprint dimensions and render with an amber halo scaled by footprint width rather than masquerading as crisp 375 m detections.

Pillar 3 — Time Delays (Δt) & Overpass-Aware False-Alarm Gating

- Regime A (Coincident Dual): Within MODIS GIFOV and |Δt| <= 90 min nominal (<= 3 h under orbital drift). Tier 1 (Dual-Confirmed): Promoted to 375 m VIIRS coordinates; 1 km MODIS parent suppressed; FRP ratio recorded.

- Regime B (Diurnal Bridged): 90 min < |Δt| <= 5.5 h within kinematic spread distance (GIFOV + 0.5 km/h x Δt). Tier 1 (Diurnal Bridged t0+Δt): Links Terra morning (~10:30 LT) and afternoon VIIRS (~13:30 LT); anchors initial ignition timestamp t0 while locking 375 m spatial coordinate to VIIRS.

- Regime C (Sub-Resolution VIIRS): Solo VIIRS (nominal/high), no MODIS corroboration. Tier 2 (VIIRS 375m Solo): Retained as small/cool/under-canopy active front missed by 1 km MODIS.

- Regime C (MODIS Gap-Fill): Solo MODIS (>= 30%), no VIIRS overpass within ±60 min & 35 km. Tier 3 (MODIS 1km Gap-Fill): Preserved to capture fast agricultural burns or cloud gaps between VIIRS passes.

- Regime C (Demoted MODIS Anomaly): Solo MODIS uncorroborated while a VIIRS overpass covered within ±60 min & 35 km. Tier 4 (Demoted / Low-Conf): Retained for full transparency, excluded from active pulsing, dimmed to 0.42 opacity.

- Low-Confidence Filter: MODIS < 30% or VIIRS low confidence. Tier 4 (Below Cross-Sensor Threshold): Toggleable in the Harmonization Filter without polluting statistical calibration.

PIPE B: THREE TRACKER TABS, VIIRS ML MODELS & PAST-FIRE t0 HINDCASTS

1. Three Isolated 14-Day Tracker Runs:

- SSOT · HARMONIZED: Tracks unified events, attaches VIIRS ML forecasts strictly to VIIRS-backed events, and records per-fire SSOT provenance (primary regime, MODIS corroboration count, FRP ratio, and max scan footprint).

- VIIRS · ML: Pure S-NPP / NOAA-20 / NOAA-21 track powering hazard and spread inference.

- MODIS: Pure Terra/Aqua track with ML predictions disabled so VIIRS-trained ML weights are never misapplied to 1 km MODIS centroids.

2. Canonical SSOT Point Structure:

- Preserves coordinates, radiative power, sensor origin, acquisition and extinction timestamps, ordinal confidence tier, satellite, corroborating matches, tracked fire ID, and trailing SSOT footprint/regime diagnostics across both recent (<=12h) and full 14-day lookback windows.

3. VIIRS-Calibrated Hazard Rating & Spread Models (12–24h):

- Hazard Rating (0–100): Composite of Fire behaviour (0.52), Terrain & fuel (0.33), and Previous-day Weather (0.15) across five bands (Low < 19, Moderate 19–25, High 26–37, Very High 38–54, Extreme >= 55).

- Model 1 — Persistence (HistGradientBoostingClassifier) · Model 2 — Expansion (>= 1 km² and >= 25% area growth, P >= 0.0845 alert threshold) · Model 3 — Additional Area Envelope (10th / median / 90th-percentile isotropic growth by fire type).

4. Past Fire Hindcast Validation:

- Rewinds past/multi-pass fires (>12h) to their earliest orbital pass (t0), evaluates model predictions from that initial state, and renders Initial Pass (t0), Observed Actual Spread, and Model Predicted Spread + 90% Bound directly on the 3D globe.

INTERACTIVE FIRE ACTIVITY CALENDAR VIEW, FILTERS & CSV EXPORTS

- Two Synchronized Calendar Views:

- 14D DAILY SSOT: 7-column interactive grid showing day-of-week headers, orbital drift flags, single-day click filtering, Shift+click date-range selection, MULTI-DAY toggle, and quick presets (All 14d, Active, Clear). Date selections synchronize bi-directionally with the timeline controls so map hotspots and tracked fires filter live.

- 2001–26 MONTHxYEAR: Scrollable 26-year heatmap (MODIS era 2001–2011 and Overlap era 2012–2026) with era filters (2001–26, 2012+ Overlap, 2001–11 MODIS), Peak>=P80 preset, clickable year rows and month columns, a pinned MED historical baseline row, and green borders distinguishing live/queried FIRMS cells from seasonal regional baseline cells.

- Four Scientific Metric Modes:

- MODIS-EQ (Cividis scale) · FRP (MW) · ANOM (diverging blue–slate–amber–red vs. median) · SSOT / ERA (3-regime daily breakdown bar or historical sensor-era key), paired with a live Selection Summary strip (SCOPE, MODIS-EQ SUM, PEAK PERIOD, TOTAL FRP / DET).

- Dual Scientific CSV Exports (with Methods Note Provenance Headers):

- Export Selected Calendar CSV: Exports selected (or all) 14D DAILY SSOT rows (MODIS-equivalent cell-days, 90% prediction intervals, canonical SSOT FRP, regime counts, and orbital drift flags) or selected 2001–26 MONTHxYEAR cells (era, data provenance, historical month median, anomaly ratio, and percentile).

- Export Selected Hotspots CSV: Exports canonical SSOT detections filtered to the active calendar selection (SSOT tier, regime, scan and track dimensions, MODIS-to-VIIRS FRP ratio, matched corroborations, overpass family, and tracked fire ID).

SCHEMATICS for ESP32 based hardware interface / Physical alert system:


The field early-warning hardware unit is built around an ESP32 (WROOM-32) microcontroller paired with a DS3231 Real-Time Clock (RTC) that maintains precise timekeeping to trigger automated API requests to the platform's harmonized fire-tracking and ML forecasting endpoints at 30-minute intervals. Upon receiving the latest hazard ratings, persistence probabilities, and predicted spread envelopes, the ESP32 cross-references the incoming fire coordinates against the unit's local position (via onboard GPS or configured station coordinates) to evaluate whether an active or high-probability fire falls within its designated danger radius particularly in remote areas where manual ground verification is impractical. When a nearby or high-hazard threat is detected, the system immediately triggers local visual and audible alarms (LED and buzzer/speaker), dispatches automated alerts to nearby authorities and first responders (via SIM800L GSM / network telemetry), and renders the fire's coordinates, hazard status, and projected spread perimeter on an onboard OLED/TFT display, which operators can navigate and inspect using a 4×4 matrix keypad.
